author: Unreal Engine
description:
GPU DEFORMERS UE5: Cartoony Squash & Stretch Effects (Sculpt & Lattice): Explore Unreal Engine's powerful and fast GPU Deformers used for adding cosmetic and dynamic changes to skeletal meshes. Focus on the Sculpt Deformer, which uses a localized sphere and handle to create fun, cartoony effects like impacts, and the Lattice Deformer for warping and skewing a character within a controlled box. Understand how these effects are generally applied late in the animation process and how the Camera Space Lattice can be used to create camera-perspective squash and stretch
►Download the A-COM Animation Sample here: https://epic.gm/agora-animation-sample
► Check out Sir Wade's channel for more Animation Tutorials and UE5 workflows: https://www.youtube.com/@SirWade/
► Sir Wade's Courses: https://courses.sirwade.com
title: Cartoony Animation! UE5 GPU Deformers (Sculpt & Lattice)

author: Unreal Engine
description:
Watch VFX Supervisor Michael Ralla and Visualization Supervisor Pepe Valencia discuss how Unreal Engine was used on ‘Sinners’ to plan demanding sequences, including a one-take music number and a large-scale train arrival, enabling creative and technical decisions to be made ahead of time.

This fireside chat with Epic’s Miles Perkins explores how the team leaned into a real-time visualization workflow built around Unreal Engine, using it not purely as a previs tool, but as a shared creative space where ideas could be explored, challenged, and aligned upon long before cameras rolled.

To learn about filmmaking in Unreal Engine, check out our website:  unrealengine.com/uses/film-television

#Sinners, #WarnerBros, #Barraboom!, #UnrealEngine, #Previs, #Filmmaking, #RealTimeVisualization, #VirtualProduction
title: Fireside Chat: Inside Sinners with Michael Ralla and Pepe Valencia

author: Unreal Engine
description:
Watch this video for a glimpse at experiences built on Qualcomm Technologies’ Snapdragon Cockpit Elite and Snapdragon Ride Elite platforms, showcasing the power of Unreal Engine’s Lumen global illumination system combined with a Qualcomm Adreno GPU and AI capabilities.

Their Snapdragon Digital Chassis concept car features multiple built-in AI agents that can answer user questions, help to solve problems, and proactively perform various tasks within the cabin. 

With hardware-enabled ray tracing, Qualcomm Technologies is also able to achieve incredibly high-fidelity rendering for the in-cabin visuals using Lumen for realistic lighting and shadows. It’s also possible to customize the displays with different themes—including a Fortnite one!

Find out more about creating automotive human-machine interfaces with Unreal Engine here: unrealengine.com/uses/hmi
